extracted.intended_audience: Qualified Health Plan (QHP) issuers, State Exchanges, accrediting entities, and regulatory/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and enforcement standards governing qualified health plan (QHP) participation, provider access (including essential community providers), accreditation consistency, audits/compliance reviews, remedies (civil money penalties and decertification), payment/netting processes, and administrative appeal procedures under Exchange regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plan exceptions process
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of an exceptions process under the non-network plan for enrollees who cannot find providers (including ECPs) willing to accept the benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies must provide an exceptions pathway for enrollees when no providers in the area (including essential community providers) will accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full; this is part of non-network plan provider access expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plan customer service and directory assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-network plan's strategy for providing adequate customer service or online provider directory assistance resources to assist plan enrollees and potential enrollees in finding providers (including ECPs) in their area who will accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must maintain customer service and online directory resources sufficient to help enrollees locate providers who will accept plan payment amounts; strategies should meaningfully assist enrollees who otherwise cannot find accepting providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider access standards for accreditation consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The provider access standards for accreditation used by recognized accrediting entities must, at a minimum, be consistent with the general requirements for network plans codified in §156.230(a)(2) and (3) and the general requirements for non-network plans codified in §156.236(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accrediting entities' standards cannot be weaker than the statutory/regulatory general requirements; accrediting standards should align with the specific network and non-network provider access provisions referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider access must include essential community providers (ECPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provider access expectations explicitly include availability of providers, including ECPs (essential community providers), in the service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network and non-network plan provider access demonstrations and enforcement include consideration of access to ECPs; failure to ensure ECP access is a compliance concern and can form the basis of enforcement actions or decertification.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS audit and compliance review authority
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS or its designee may audit or conduct a compliance review of an issuer offering a QHP through an Exchange to assess its compliance with the applicable requirements related to administration of the advance payments of the premium tax credit, cost-sharing reductions, and user fee programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS-initiated audits/compliance reviews target administration of APTC, CSRs, and program user fees; these reviews are formal processes used to assess issuer compliance with applicable administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance reviews conducted under this section will follow the standards set forth in §156.715.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance review procedures, scope, and technical standards are governed by §156.715; issuers subject to review should expect reviews to adhere to those standards and prepare records accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances triggering HHS enforcement for APTC/CSR/user fee administration
rubrics_metrics.description: If HHS determines that the State Exchange or State-based Exchange on the Federal platform is not enforcing or fails to substantially enforce compliance with the applicable requirements related to administration of the advance payments of the premium tax credit, cost-sharing reductions, and user fee programs, then HHS may do so and may pursue the imposition of civil money penalties as specified in §156.805 for noncompliance by QHP issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS may step in to enforce program administration when States fail to do so; this can include pursuing CMPs against issuers in the relevant Exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sanctions under subpart I
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions under subpart I are applicable for noncompliance with QHP issuer participation standards and other standards applicable to issuers offering QHPs in a Federally-facilitated Exchange; sanctions under paragraph (a)(1) are also applicable for noncompliance by QHP issuers participating in State Exchanges and State-based Exchanges on the Federal platform when HHS is responsible for enforcement of any of the requirements identified in §156.805(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions apply broadly to FFE issuers and can apply to issuers in State Exchanges or SBEs on the Federal platform when HHS has enforcement responsibility—issuers should be aware sanctions reach beyond FFEs in those circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors in determining amount of civil money penalties (CMPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the amount of civil money penalties, HHS will identify the lawful purpose or purposes of the civil money penalty, and take into account the following factors as appropriate to the circumstances of the case (see §156.805(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS uses a factor-based assessment to set CMP amounts; while the full list of factors appears in the regulation, the rule requires HHS to identify purposes and weigh factors appropriate to each case when calculating penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring HHS enforcement in State Exchanges and SBEs on Federal platform
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will enforce the requirements applicable to the actions identified in paragraph (a) of §156.805 that are applicable to issuers offering a QHP in a State Exchange or State-based Exchange on the Federal platform if the State with enforcement authority notifies HHS that it is not enforcing these requirements or if HHS makes a determination using the process set forth at 45 CFR 150.201 et seq. that such State is failing to substantially enforce these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers for HHS enforcement in State-run Exchanges include state notification of non-enforcement or an HHS determination via the specified process; once HHS assumes enforcement responsibility it may impose CMPs per §156.805.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for imposing CMPs on issuers in State Exchanges when HHS enforces
rubrics_metrics.description: If HHS is responsible for enforcement of the requirements applicable to actions identified in §156.805 for issuers offering a QHP in a State Exchange or SBE on the Federal platform, HHS may impose civil money penalties on an issuer in such Exchange in accordance with the bases and process set forth in §156.805.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When HHS enforces in State Exchanges, it follows §156.805's bases and process for CMP imposition; issuers in such Exchanges are subject to the same CMP frameworks as FFE issuers under those circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decertification grounds for QHPs related to provider access
rubrics_metrics.description: A QHP issuer substantially fails to meet the requirements under §156.230 related to provider access standards for network plans, §156.235 related to essential community provider access standards for network plans, or §156.236 related to provider access and essential community providers standards for non-network plans, as applicable; this substantial failure is a basis for decertification of a QHP offered by an issuer through a Federally-facilitated Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial failures to meet the cited provider access or ECP access standards can lead to decertification; issuers should maintain compliance with those specific sections to avoid decertification risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ subpoena authority and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The ALJ, upon his or her own motion or at the request of a party, may issue subpoenas if they are reasonably necessary for the full presentation of a case. A party must file a written request for a subpoena with the ALJ at least 5 calendar days before the date set for the hearing. The request must (i) identify the witnesses or documents to be produced; (ii) describe their addresses or location with sufficient particularity to permit them to be found; and (iii) specify the pertinent facts the party expects to establish by the witnesses or documents, and indicate why those facts could not be established without use of a subpoena. Subpoenas are issued in the name of the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoena requests must be timely (≥5 calendar days before hearing) and substantively justify the need; ALJs can also issue subpoenas sua sponte when reasonably necessary; subpoenas are formal and issued in the Secretary's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery exception for appeals of civil money penalties from audits/compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: This discovery section does not apply to appeals of civil money penalties imposed under §156.805 for violations identified during audits or compliance reviews conducted in accordance with §156.480(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals of CMPs based on audit/compliance review findings have limited discovery rights under this provision; parties should consult the specific discovery rules and exceptions applicable to such appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS netting authority for payments and charges
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of its payment and collections process, HHS may net payments owed to issuers and their affiliates operating under the same tax identification number against amounts due to the Federal Government from the issuers and their affiliates under the same taxpayer identification number for advance payments of the premium tax credit, advance payments of and reconciliation of cost-sharing reductions, payment of Federally-facilitated Exchange user fees, payment of State Exchanges utilizing the Federal platform user fees, HHS risk adjustment, reinsurance, and risk corridors payments and charges, administrative fees for utilizing the Federal Independent Dispute Resolution process in accordance with §149.510(d)(2), and civil money penalties assessed for violations of any applicable Exchange standards and requirements or Public Health Service Act standards and requirements applicable to issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS can offset amounts owed to issuers against a comprehensive list of federal program liabilities; issuers and affiliates under a common TIN should plan for potential netting across these program payments and charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of debt after netting
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amount owed to the Federal Government by an issuer and its affiliates for advance payments of the premium tax credit, advance payments of and reconciliation of cost-sharing reductions, Federally-facilitated Exchange user fees (including fees for State-based Exchanges utilizing the Federal platform), HHS risk adjustment, reinsurance, risk corridors, unpaid administrative fees for utilizing the Federal Independent Dispute Resolution process, and civil money penalties assessed for violations of applicable Exchange or PHS Act requirements, after HHS nets amounts owed by the Federal Government under these programs, is a determination of a debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After netting, remaining amounts are formally treated as a debt subject to Federal debt collection authorities and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and timing for request for informal administrative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an informal hearing must be made in writing and filed with HHS within 30 calendar days of the date of the reconsideration decision under paragraph (a)(6) of this section. If the last day of this period is not a business day, the request for an informal hearing must be made in writing and filed by the next applicable business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 30-calendar-day filing deadline (with basic business day adjustment) governs informal hearing requests following reconsideration decisions; requests must be in writing and timely to preserve appeal rights.
